## events (48)

- **fox_in_the_snare** (verses [1]): A Fox in the Snare. A white fox kit is tangled in a hunter's snare, one bell-tipped tail thrashing. It has stopped struggling and started glaring, which is either a very good sign or a very bad one. Choices: [Loosen the snare | Hurts the front hero] [Sell it to the hunter | A curse: Regret] [Leave it. Not your fable.]
- **kappa_toll** (verses [1]): The Kappa Wants a Toll. A kappa sits on a mossy bridge, water dish gleaming. 'Toll,' he says. 'Twenty gold, or a cucumber, or a very good reason.' He is small, damp, and completely serious about it. Choices: [Pay the twenty gold | 20 gold] [Bow. Very, very deeply. | He may not bow back] [Mention the fox you helped] [Take the long way round]
- **tanuki_tea_house** (verses [1]): Tea, Allegedly. A tanuki in a tiny apron runs a tea stall between two bamboo stalks. The sign says TEA (REAL). The tanuki says the sign is not lying, which is somehow worse. Choices: [Pay for a proper pot | 25 gold] [Pay with a leaf | Maybe 25 gold] [Let Kuro read the menu] [Admire the teapots]
- **hanae_mirror_pool** (verses [1]): Hanae's Reflection. A still pool shows Hanae her reflection. It has better posture and a slightly smug ponytail, and it draws first. Hanae, very calmly, decides to take this personally. Choices: [Let her duel it | Hanae will be hurt] [Bow and walk on]
- **mushroom_ring** (verses [1]): The Mushroom Ring. Mushroom folk dance in a ring of tiny caps and beckon you closer. The ring smells of rain, wet earth, and a rumour you cannot quite place. One of them is holding out a cap. Choices: [Dance with them | A card changes, spores sting] [Eat the offered cap | Could go either way] [Decline politely]
- **jizo_row** (verses [1]): The Seventh Jizo. Seven moss-capped jizo line the path, each wearing a faded red bib. Six are smiling. The seventh frowns at nothing, and has been left a whole bowl of rice. Choices: [Leave an offering | 20 gold] [Take the rice | Maybe a curse: Doubt] [Tie on a fresh bib]
- **tengu_dice** (verses [1]): The Tengu's Dice. A crow tengu sits on a stump with three dice and an enormous hat. 'Even or odd,' he offers. 'Fifty gold a throw, and I only cheat a little.' The dice look extremely well-loved. Choices: [Bet fifty gold on even | Up to 50 gold] [Ask Kuro about the dice] [Let Hanae challenge him to a real duel] [Watch him play a round]
- **stone_lantern_story** (verses [1]): The Lantern Wants a Song. An old stone lantern, unlit for a century, says it will shine if someone sings it a song. It would like a good one. It has already heard most of the others. Choices: [Sing it a song] [Let Kuro play it a tune] [Light it yourself | 1 Echo]
- **oni_cub_sumo** (verses [1]): The Oni Cub Wants a Match. An oni cub in a very small loincloth slaps the ground and points at you. He wants a match. The whole grove has gone quiet to watch. He is enormously, dangerously sincere. Choices: [Accept the match (fight)] [Let Raiga step into the ring] [Slip him a rice ball | 10 gold] [Slip away quietly]
- **hermit_brush_seller** (verses [1]): The Hermit's Songs. A hermit in a bamboo hut sells songs of every length, all of them a little out of breath. 'They are single use,' she says, 'like most good ideas.' She looks at your deck with interest. Choices: [Buy a Ripple | 60 gold] [Trade a card for a song | Lose a card, 70 gold] [Just talk]
- **paper_kodama_pilgrim** (verses [1]): The Kodama's Echo. A hollow kodama shuffles along the road with one small echo cupped in its hands. It has no voice of its own. When it sees you it stops, and holds the echo out with both hands. Choices: [Listen to the echo | It may sour your deck] [Ask it to echo a card | 40 gold] [Pat its head]
- **missing_page** (verses [1]): A Door of Silence. In the middle of the grove hangs a doorway of perfect silence, grey and still. The bamboo leans away from it. Something is missing here, and you can feel it like a lost tooth. Choices: [Step around it] [Reach in | Something may change] [Sing into it | 2 Echo, maybe a curse]
- **fox_returns** (verses [2]): The Fox on the Bridge. A white fox with two tails, one tipped with a tiny bell, waits on a mossy bridge post. She looks exactly like a kit you once untangled, only taller, and she is holding a small carved mask in her mouth. Choices: [Accept the mask | Hurts the front hero] [Follow her across the rooftops] [Ask her about Kuzunoha] [Scratch her behind the ears]
- **lantern_ferry** (verses [2]): The Lantern Ferry. The ferryman is a paper lantern on a pole, steering a boat of folded paper. Fare is thirty gold, he says. Or one song. Or, if you are honest, one thing you are afraid of. Choices: [Pay the fare | 30 gold] [Swim it | Cold water] [Say the fox sent you] [Tell him your fear]
- **endless_supper** (verses [2]): The Endless Supper. A long table under paper lanterns, laid for supper. The guests are pale and polite and will not stop chewing. 'Sit,' says a voice from everywhere. 'Every guest stays for supper.' Choices: [Sit and eat | May leave a curse: Burden] [Slip into the kitchen (risky)] [Decline politely]
- **puppet_theatre** (verses [2]): The Puppet Theatre. A tiny theatre, curtains parted. Paper puppets act out a familiar scene: two heroes, a bridge, a fox. The puppet heroes have your faces. Someone is pulling the strings, and they are late with the ending. Choices: [Step onto the stage | A card is recast] [Cut the strings (risky)] [Watch until the end]
- **koi_wishing_pond** (verses [2]): The Wishing Pond. A koi pond glows faintly beneath a sign: WISHES, 10 GOLD. Under it, in different handwriting: ALSO WE ARE JUDGING YOU. A very old carp watches you with real attention. Choices: [Make a wish | 10 gold] [Fish out the coins | A curse: Hex] [Make an honest wish, no coin]
- **pawn_shop** (verses [2]): The Pawnshop of Objects. A pawnshop where every object is awake and none of them enjoy it. An umbrella whispers 'take me,' a teapot mutters 'don't,' and the abacus keeps score of everything. Choices: [Sell a card | Maybe a curse] [Buy a mystery object | 60 gold] [Talk to the teapot]
- **flooded_archive** (verses [2]): The Flooded Music Hall. A flooded music hall, knee-deep in black water. Drums float upside down, their skins gone slack. On the top shelf one flute is still dry, and humming to itself. Choices: [Wade in for the dry flute | The water bites] [Let Kuro listen to the shelves] [Shake out a drowned flute]
- **kuro_footnote** (verses [2]): Kuro's Harmony. Kuro stops beside a broken music box and goes very still. It is playing his harmony, the quiet line under the melody, in a voice he knows better than his own. He has not heard the end. Not yet. Choices: [Let him listen] [Ask him to sing along] [Hum a harmony of your own | 1 Echo]
- **sentry_bridge** (verses [2]): The Sentry Who Was Never Relieved. A drowned soldier guards the last bridge, spear upright, water streaming from his armour. 'Halt,' he says. 'Password.' Nobody has given him one in three hundred years. Choices: [Say, "You are relieved, soldier."] [Guess a password | It may hurt] [Duel him for the bridge (fight)] [Let Hanae offer a duel of honour]
- **mask_market** (verses [2]): The Night Market of Masks. A night market of masks: fox, oni, plain white. Every vendor wears a face that is not theirs. 'Try one,' they say, in a chorus that has clearly been rehearsed. 'It never comes off wrong.' Choices: [Try a plain white mask | It may not come off right] [Show your fox mask] [Buy nothing]
- **silk_threads** (verses [2]): Threads Across the Alley. Silk threads hang across the alley, each tied to something: a lantern, a shoe, a wedding ring. They tremble all together, as though something far away has just noticed you. Choices: [Cut a thread | Something will notice] [Untie the wedding ring | Hurts the front hero] [Follow one thread]
- **rokurokubi_gossip** (verses [2]): A Word from the Tea House. A lady sits in a tea house window, very still and very far away. Her neck extends, politely, across the room to whisper in your ear. 'I know a shortcut,' she says. 'Nobody uses it twice.' Choices: [Buy the shortcut | 20 gold] [Ask for medicinal tea] [Trade gossip]
- **fox_at_the_gate** (verses [3]): Three Tails at the Gate. Three white tails, one tipped with a tiny bell, curl around a broken gargoyle. The fox has grown. She sings one clear note at the gate stone, and it hums back a door, and then, faintly, HURRY. Choices: [Step through her door] [Let her mend you] [Take her pawprint] [Ask her for something bigger]
- **kill_your_darlings** (verses [3]): Notes from the Podium. A rehearsal hall, chairs in neat rows. From an empty podium a dry voice gives notes on a loop. Too loud. Too slow. Cut the solo. Then, clearly about your party: NEEDS WORK. Choices: [Cut your favourite solo | Lose a card and 8 HP] [Play it, do not explain | Hurts the front hero] [Give a note of your own]
- **unfinished_sentence** (verses [3]): The Unfinished Song. In a ruined room a music box sings one line and stops mid-word: 'And then the hero, who had never once been afraid, s'. A flute lies on the floor, still warm. The rest is silence. Choices: [Finish it bravely | Hurts the front hero] [Finish it kindly] [Finish it cleverly] [Leave it unfinished]
- **void_tear** (verses [3]): A Tear in the Sky. A tear in the sky, grey and perfectly silent. Sounds drift toward it and vanish: a bird's call, a bell, half of a laugh. The wind smells of nothing. Nothing, it turns out, has a very specific smell. Choices: [Step through | Deck clutter] [Feed it something you regret] [Back away slowly]
- **lightning_rod** (verses [3]): The Lightning Rod. A brass lightning rod stands at the cliff edge, humming. The storm bends toward it like a cat toward a lap. It is either an invitation or a very bad idea. Probably both. Choices: [Take the hit | Storm damage] [Let Raiga hold it] [Bottle some lightning | A little damage] [Ground the rod]
- **censor_office** (verses [3]): The Office of Silence. A tidy desk in a storm. A clerk with a felt gag where his mouth should be stamps a form, reads it, stamps it again. 'Request for silence?' he mimes. 'Take a number. Or a stamp. Nobody is sure.' Choices: [File Form 27-B (Request to Be Forgotten) | Lose a card, 60 gold] [Argue with the clerk (risky)] [Leave quietly]
- **library_cat** (verses [3]): The Cat on the Koto. In the ruins of a great music hall, a very fat cat sits on the last koto, washing one paw. The Hush has eaten the hall around it. It has not eaten the cat. It has clearly not tried. Choices: [Pet the cat] [Share your rations | 10 gold] [Move the cat (risky)]
- **weeping_eraser** (verses [3]): The Wraith That Cannot Stop. A muffle wraith kneels in a ring of grey dust, weeping without a sound. Everything it touches goes silent, so it has tried very hard to touch nothing. It has, by now, run out of nothing. Choices: [Sit with it] [Let Suzu sing to it] [Take what it is holding (fight)]
- **suzu_cracked_binding** (verses [3]): Suzu Hears the Strings. Suzu stops, one hand held against the air, listening. Deep under the stone, something huge is humming out of tune, string by string. 'It is the song itself,' she says quietly. 'It is coming loose. I think I can hold it.' Choices: [Let Suzu hold it] [Help her tighten the strings | String burn for both] [Leave it to the Singer]
- **komainu_riddle** (verses [3]): The Two Gates. Two stone komainu flank a gate, one mouth open, one shut. 'One of us always lies,' says one. 'The other lies about something else,' says the other. 'Choose a gate,' they add, unhelpfully. Choices: [Try the left gate | A coin flip] [Try the right gate | A coin flip] [Let Kuro ask one question] [Climb the wall]
- **paper_boat_prayers** (verses [3]): A Sea of Paper Boats. Thousands of paper boats drift through the storm clouds, each carrying a candle and a tiny bell, every candle out, every bell still. Somebody folded them all by hand, in one night. They are waiting. Choices: [Light one | 1 Echo] [Ring the bells] [Take a boat for the road]
- **waiting_room** (verses [3]): Please Wait To Be Auditioned. A pristine waiting room with a ticket dispenser and a single chair. The sign says PLEASE WAIT TO BE AUDITIONED. The chair is warm. Your ticket says you are number one. Choices: [Take a ticket | It may leave a mark] [Bribe the receptionist | 40 gold] [Sit in the chair]
- **peddler_silver_bell** (verses undefined): The Peddler and the Bell. A peddler with a pack taller than he is lays out his wares: three jars, a brass lamp, and an empty string knotted for a bell. He does not sell so much as suggest. 'Everything is for sale,' he says. Choices: [Buy the mystery bundle | 80 gold] [Buy the brass lamp | 60 gold] [Ring your silver bell] [Just talk]
- **jade_door** (verses undefined): The Jade Door. A jade-green door stands alone in the middle of the road, with no wall around it and a lock the exact shape of your key. It hums when you come near, like a cat that has recognised its owner. Choices: [Open it] [Knock first]
- **brass_lantern_secret** (verses undefined): The Lantern Leans. Your brass lantern flickers, then leans, unmistakably, toward an ordinary-looking stretch of wall. It has never leaned before. It has the air of a lantern that has been waiting for you to ask. Choices: [Follow the lantern] [Ask it nicely]
- **wandering_storyteller** (verses undefined): The Storyteller. A storyteller sits under a paper umbrella and pats the mat beside her. 'A tale for a coin,' she says, 'or a coin for a tale. I am flexible about the direction.' Choices: [Pay for a story | 20 gold] [Let Kuro correct her rhythm] [Ask how it all ends] [Tell her a story]
- **hungry_ghost** (verses undefined): The Hungry Ghost. A hungry ghost sits at the crossroads beside an empty bowl. It does not beg. It only sits there being empty, and somehow that is worse. Choices: [Fill the bowl | 45 gold] [Share your rations | Both heroes go hungry] [Walk on]
- **strange_seed** (verses undefined): A Seed in the Light. A single seed sits on a stone in a beam of light. It is the wrong colour for any plant, and faintly warm, as though someone held it a moment ago and was called away. Choices: [Plant it | It might bite] [Keep it in your pocket | Hurts the front hero] [Leave it in the light]
- **two_doors** (verses undefined): The Honest Door and the Kind One. Two doors stand side by side on the road, both wearing name tags. The left one says I WILL TELL YOU THE TRUTH. The right one says YOU LOOK WONDERFUL. Neither has a wall attached. Choices: [The honest door] [The kind door] [Try the small door at the back] [Neither]
- **weary_travellers** (verses undefined): Three Travellers and a Pot. Three travellers share a small fire and a smaller pot of soup. They wave you over without asking who you are, which, in a song, is either great trust or great foreshadowing. Choices: [Take the first watch] [Trade for a song | 25 gold] [Share the fire]
- **blank_patch** (verses undefined): The Patch of Silence. A patch of the road has gone grey. Not fog: nothing. A cricket hops into it and stops mid-chirp. The edge of it is advancing, slowly, like a very patient tide. Choices: [Sing it back | 2 Echo] [Let Suzu seal the edge] [Throw in a cursed card] [Step around it]
- **scribes_bargain** (verses undefined): The Busker of Small Fates. A tiny busker, drumming a beat on an upturned bowl, offers to sing your fate a new line for a small fee. 'One line,' he says. 'Anything you like. No refunds, no encores, and not the ending.' Choices: [A line for the body | 25 gold] [A line for the purse | It may backfire] [Cut a line | Lose a card] [Decline the song]
- **raiga_storm_laugh** (verses undefined): Raiga's Laugh. Raiga throws back his head and laughs for no reason at all, and everything within earshot laughs with him. The Hush, which had been creeping toward the path, stops. It seems, for a moment, to be listening. Choices: [Laugh with him] [Ask what is so funny] [Dare him to laugh louder | Thunder may answer] [Bottle the echo]
- **paper_crane_folder** (verses undefined): A Thousand Paper Cranes. An old woman folds paper cranes, and her fingers never seem to hurry. A thousand lie at her feet. She has, she says, nearly finished. She has been nearly finished for a very long time. Choices: [Ask for a wish] [Help her fold]

## lore (16)

- **intro**: Once, a Song. Once there was a land that sang itself. Its Singer had loved it so long and so well that one day the song simply kept going without a voice. Then, on an ordinary night, just before the last note, a small doubt whispered that it might come out wrong, and the Singer held a breath and did not let it go
- **ch1_intro**: The Whispering Bamboo Grove. The first verse smells of rain and warm cedar. The Whispering Bamboo Grove glows in golden dusk, every stalk murmuring the tune it is afraid to forget. Kodama answer every call, one beat late. A kappa guards a bridge with terrible manners. And somewhere in the middle, a white fox with nine ringing t
- **ch1_clear**: The Fox Lowers Her Voice. Kuzunoha's nine tails drooped one by one, like bells with the ringing gone out of them. The song ran out of her, and the wildness with it, and she sat down in the bamboo, very small for a fox the size of a house. 'I was only trying to keep it,' she said. 'Every time the Hush ate a note, I sang two m
- **ch2_intro**: The Sunken Lantern City. The second verse is played in lantern light on black water. The Sunken Lantern City drifts under a sky like a folded kimono, every canal lined with paper lamps and every lamp watching. Once this was a festival town, and the festival never stopped: now the drums are slack and the flutes are full of w
- **ch2_clear**: The Threads Come Loose. When the last silk thread snapped, the city did not fall. It exhaled. Jorogumo sat among the wreck of her kimono, fingers still tying knots in nothing. 'The Hush was going to eat them,' she said. 'The guests, the lamps, the music, all of them. So I kept them. I kept them here.' Nobody answered, beca
- **ch3_intro**: The Thunderless Citadel. The last verse is not sung at all. It is conducted. The Thunderless Citadel hangs above a sea of storm cloud, its bells wrapped in grey felt, its halls lined with instruments whose strings have been cut. Lightning strikes in neat, careful lines, and no thunder follows. Through the window slits the s
- **victory**: The Final Chorus. The Conductor lowered his red baton, and his face came apart like a held breath let go. 'It had to be perfect,' he whispered, in the Singer's own tired voice. 'A wrong note can never be unsung, so I never let one come.' The Singer had not vanished. The Singer had only stopped believing the last note
- **defeat**: A Rest in the Music. The echoes thinned. The bamboo, the lanterns, the storm, all of it went grey and soft, and the heroes heard their own voices fade to nothing. It did not hurt. That was the worst part. The Hush is polite that way. But a song that sings itself does not stay silent for long, and a rest is not the end o
- **hero_hanae**: Hanae, the Blossom Blade. The Singer sang Hanae on the very first bar, on a day the Singer felt brave. She was meant to be the hero: the one who steps forward first, so the rest of the song has somewhere to stand. She has a very good ponytail, an even better blade, and a reputation for never missing her cue. Every cut she ma
- **hero_kuro**: Kuro, the Songweaver. Kuro began as a harmony. The Singer needed someone to carry the tune where the melody could not reach, so a quiet second line was hummed under the first, glasses and all, and then, because the Singer was kind, given a personality. It got out of hand. He is the only one who knows he lives in a song, 
- **hero_suzu**: Suzu, the Moon Miko. The Singer sang Suzu late at night, on the evenings when the song would not come. She is the shrine at the edge of the map, the bell left ringing for whoever is lost. She keeps the song in tune: every slack string, every note gone sour, she feels in her hair, and she mends what she can without makin
- **hero_raiga**: Raiga, the Thunder Monk. Raiga was sung in a thunderstorm by a Singer who was laughing too hard to hold the note. He was meant to be the comic relief. He declined. He takes every blow with a grin and returns it louder, and his thunder is not lightning at all but a laugh, the Singer's own, caught in the song and never let go

## tips (30)

- tip 1: Waking a hex costs Echo. Temple bells, kills and Meditate at camp all give it back.
- tip 2: Songs wake whole shapes for free. Save the long ones for when the boss is far away.
- tip 3: You can only walk on woken hexes, but you can wake far ahead: the game finds the cheapest chain for you.
- tip 4: The front hero takes most of the attacks. The back hero is safer, but some cards only shine up front.
- tip 5: One row swap per turn is free. Every extra swap costs Energy, so plan the second one.
- tip 6: A downed hero is not gone. Their cards clog your hand until the fight is won and they stand up again.
- tip 7: If both heroes fall, the journey ends. Keep the front hero healthy and the back hero alive.
- tip 8: Block wears off at the start of your next turn. Spend it or lose it.
- tip 9: Enemy intents show what they will do next. Read them before you play your first card.
- tip 10: Vulnerable makes an enemy take much more damage. Apply it first, then swing.
- tip 11: Weak trims an enemy's next attacks. Against a boss with a big hit coming, it is a small shield.
- tip 12: Poison ignores Block. It is slow, but nothing can defend against it, which makes it wonderful against armour.
- tip 13: Bind stops both heroes from swapping. Keep a plan that works without a swap.
- tip 14: Gems only fit slots of their own colour. A prism slot takes any colour.
- tip 15: Red gems sharpen attacks, blue bolster Block and healing, green bend the rules, gold do a bit of everything.
- tip 16: Replacing a socketed gem destroys the old one. Be sure before you cut.
- tip 17: Camps offer Rest, Sharpen, Cut Gems or Meditate, one per visit. Forges do Sharpen or Cut Gems.
- tip 18: A power that says "either hero" counts your ally's cards too. One that says "you" counts only its own hero.
- tip 19: Shops sell card removal. A leaner deck draws your best cards more often.
- tip 20: Curse cards are dead weight in your hand. A shop can remove them, and a few fables will take them away.
- tip 21: A fable is a choice, not a test. There is usually a safe option, a gamble, and a price. Pick your risk.
- tip 22: In a fable, good manners are sometimes a weapon. Try bowing to a kappa.
- tip 23: A treasure can change how you play. Read its text twice before you build around it.
- tip 24: Stranded with no Echo and no path? The land takes pity and gives you enough for one hex.
- tip 25: Most kills refill a little Echo, and elites more. Minions give none. Fighting is how you cross the land.
- tip 26: An X cost card spends all your remaining Energy. Play it last, when you know how much you have.
- tip 27: Retain keeps a card in hand at the end of a turn. Hold your finisher until you can afford it.
- tip 28: Exhaust removes a card for the rest of the fight. Powerful, but count how many you can spare.
- tip 29: Every hero hides a resource: Bloom, Breath, Ward or Charge. Learn which cards build it and which spend it.
- tip 30: Tempo Trials make the journey harder. Win one to unlock the next. The Daily Jam gives everyone the same seed.
